title: Associations between tissue stiffness, tumor response to transarterial chemoembolization and prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma: insights from multifrequency 3D-magnetic resonance elastography.
abstract: Objectives To investigate the correlation between tissue stiffness, as measured across various target tissues using multifrequency three-dimensional magnetic resonance elastography (3D-MRE), and tumor responses to transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), as well as post-treatment prognosis in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods HCC patients scheduled for TACE treatment were prospectively recruited and received multifrequency 3D-MRE before the initiation of TACE procedure. Measurements of tumor stiffness (TS), liver stiffness (LS), and spleen stiffness (SS) were conducted at frequencies of 60 Hz and 30 Hz, respectively. Treatment response was assessed using the mRECIST. Patient follow-up was conducted to evaluate overall survival outcomes. Results The final patient cohort consisted of 43 patients (mean age: 56.66±10.13 years; 34 males), including 16 non-responders and 27 responders. Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival. Conclusion Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

Non-responders exhibited significantly elevated TS (4.10±2.54 vs. 2.68±1.61kPa, p=0.035), LS (2.88±1.43 vs. 1.97±0.59kPa, p=0.026), and SS (4.03±0.90 vs. 3.13±1.08kPa, p=0.008) at the frequency of 30Hz. Firth's penalized univariable logistic analysis identified age (adjusted odds ratio [OR]=0.93, P=0.036), tumor number (OR=0.69, P=0.035), LS at 60Hz (OR=0.79, p=0.046), TS at 30Hz (OR=0.73, p=0.037), LS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, p=0.008), and SS at 30Hz (OR=0.44, P=0.009) as potential predictors of treatment response. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for predicting treatment response was 0.69 for age, tumor number and TS at 30Hz, 0.67 for LS at both 60Hz and 30Hz, and 0.75 for SS at 30Hz. Univariable Cox regression identified TS at both 60Hz (hazard ratio=1.15, p=0.014) and 30Hz (hazard ratio=1.40, p=0.010) as potential predictors of overall survival.

Conclusion

Spleen stiffness measured at 30 Hz via 3D-MRE may serve as a potential predictor of treatment response to TACE in HCC patients, whereas tumor stiffness measured at both 60Hz and 30Hz appears to correlate with overall survival. Further research is necessary to validate these preliminary associations.

title: A CAD-Based Workflow for Structured Mid-Sagittal Plane Definition in Contralateral Mandibular Mirroring: A Technical Note.
abstract: Objectives To describe a structured CAD-based workflow for defining the mandibular mid-sagittal plane during contralateral mirroring for unilateral mandibular defects and to demonstrate its clinical applicability in reconstructive planning. Methods DICOM data were segmented to generate a mandibular STL model. In CAD software, a mid-sagittal splitting plane was constructed using convergent geometric references, including a best-fit plane, principal inertia axis, and centre-of-gravity point, combined with pogonion as the anterior midline reference. The unaffected hemimandible was mirrored across this plane, exported as an STL file, and used for biomodel fabrication, guide planning, and reconstruction plate pre-contouring. A representative ameloblastoma case was used to illustrate the workflow. Results The workflow produced a mirrored mandibular template suitable for digital-to-physical transfer. In the representative case, the template supported preoperative reconstruction plate adaptation and intraoperative contour planning. At 12-month follow-up, facial contour and occlusion were clinically acceptable on qualitative assessment. Conclusions A convergent reference CAD workflow offers a practical method for standardising mid-sagittal plane definition in mandibular contralateral mirroring. The workflow may reduce reliance on subjective landmark selection in unilateral pathology; however, quantitative validation against established midplane methods is required. Clinical significance This technique provides a stepwise digital planning workflow for unilateral mandibular reconstruction, helping surgeons define the mid-sagittal plane, create mirrored templates, fabricate biomodels, and pre-contour reconstruction plates when tumour-related distortion limits reliable anatomical reference points. Level of evidence v This journal requires that authors assign a level of evidence to each article. For a full description of these Evidence-Based Medicine ratings, please refer to the Table of Contents or the online Instructions to Authors www.springer.com/00266 .

title: A short large-calibre intrapelvic arterial bridge between the superior and inferior gluteal arteries: an in vivo CT angiographic observation.
abstract: Purpose To describe a short, large-calibre intrapelvic arterial bridge between independently established superior and inferior gluteal arteries (SGA and IGA) and to distinguish it from a common gluteal trunk. Methods A pelvic computed tomography angiography (CTA) examination from a 40-year-old man was retrospectively analysed from an anonymised archive using multiplanar reformations, maximum-intensity projections, and three-dimensional vascular reconstructions. Linear and calibre measurements were obtained with workstation callipers and verified by independent review. Results On the right, the internal iliac artery divided after 34 mm into anterior and posterior trunks. The anterior trunk gave the obturator and internal pudendal arteries and continued as the IGA (2.6 mm); the posterior trunk gave sacral arteries and continued as the SGA (4.0 mm). The SGA and IGA were connected 44.2 mm distal to the internal iliac bifurcation by a 1.8-mm-long, 3.5-mm-calibre intrapelvic bridge. The SGA exited suprapiriformly and the IGA infrapiriformly. No corresponding bridge was present on the left. Conclusion The configuration differs from an Adachi Type II common SGA-IGA trunk because the two gluteal arteries are already anatomically separate before the communicating segment. Strict assignment to an Adachi type is not possible from this CTA alone because the umbilical continuation of the hypogastric axis is not demonstrated. Previous cadaveric studies documented SGA-IGA communications, whereas the present observation provides individual in vivo CTA topography and morphometry of a very short, large-calibre bridge.

title: [The eye as a mirror of the heart-retinal findings in heart failure and cardiovascular diseases].
abstract: Background Due to its unique anatomical and functional characteristics, the retina represents a promising organ for the evaluation of systemic vascular diseases. Modern imaging techniques, particularly optical coherence tomography angiography (OCT-A), enable noninvasive and quantitative assessment of retinal microcirculation. The aim of this review is to present current findings on the significance of retinal biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases, with a focus on heart failure. Results Numerous studies show associations between retinal vascular changes and arterial hypertension, coronary heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and heart failure. Changes in retinal vascular parameters such as vascular density and perfusion density correlate with structural and functional cardiac changes. Patients with retinal vascular occlusions have an increased risk of stroke, myocardial infarction, and higher cardiovascular mortality. Initial studies in patients with acute decompensated heart failure have demonstrated changes in retinal vascular and perfusion density that can be reversed by recompensation. These observations led to the introduction of the term "cardio-ocular syndrome," which describes the interactions between cardiac function, systemic congestion, and retinal microcirculation. Conclusion Retinal imaging opens up new possibilities for the noninvasive assessment of systemic microcirculatory disorders in cardiovascular diseases. OCT‑A could contribute in the future to risk stratification, assessment of disease progression, and monitoring of therapy in heart failure.

title: The boundary between microbial detection and implant-related infection: a structured narrative review of analytical credibility, biological persistence, host response, and clinical causality.
abstract: Background Unexpected microbial signals are frequently encountered in patients with orthopaedic implants who do not satisfy validated criteria for confirmed infection. The central interpretive problem is not limited to periprosthetic joint infection (PJI); it also arises in fracture-fixation and spinal instrumentation, and it involves conventional culture, sonication, histopathology, broad-range polymerase chain reaction (PCR), 16 S rRNA sequencing, and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS). Methods We performed a structured narrative review of literature identified in PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science, updated through 27 June 2026. Eligible publications addressed microbial or biofilm-associated signals in orthopaedic implants without unequivocal infection at the time of sampling, or reported outcomes after unexpected positive cultures. Evidence was organized by implant type, indication for implant removal, detection method, host-response evidence, and longitudinal outcome. Particular attention was paid to the distinction between routinely removed fracture-fixation devices and failure-related arthroplasty or spinal revisions. Results Routine removal of fracture-fixation devices provides the least confounded clinical window and demonstrates that microbial signals may be recovered from implants in the absence of recognized failure or overt infection. By contrast, arthroplasty and spinal cohorts labelled "presumed aseptic" are intrinsically confounded because pain, loosening, osteolysis, or pseudarthrosis may represent occult infection. Molecular positivity is further limited by low-biomass contamination and inability to distinguish viable organisms from relic DNA. Favorable outcomes after revision do not prove that infection was never present, because revision surgery itself may eradicate or substantially reduce an occult microbial burden. Conclusions Microbial detection should be interpreted through three sequential domains: analytical credibility, biological activity or persistence, and clinical causality supported by host response or implant-related pathology. "Stable coexistence" is best treated as a longitudinal clinical phenotype or testable mechanistic hypothesis, not as an established diagnostic category. This framework complements, but does not replace, validated PJI, fracture-related infection (FRI), or other implant-specific definitions.

title: Impact of puncture site location in percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage on outcomes of subsequent laparoscopic cholecystectomy: a multicenter retrospective clinical study.
abstract: Background Percutaneous transhepatic gallbladder drainage (PTGD) followed by laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is an effective treatment strategy for acute cholecystitis (AC). However, the impact of the PTGD puncture site on subsequent LC outcomes has not been systematically investigated. Methods This retrospective study included patients diagnosed with AC who underwent PTGD followed by LC at the First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University (January 2018-May 2025) and Yingkou Central Hospital (January 2020-May 2025). PTGD was performed according to the Tokyo Guidelines 2018 (TG18) and individualized clinical judgment. Based on CT imaging, patients were categorized into two groups according to the PTGD puncture site: the fundus group (n = 208), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder fundus, and the neck group (n = 47), where the puncture was adjacent to the gallbladder neck. Clinical parameters compared included baseline characteristics, gallbladder neck stone impaction, post-PTGD hospital stay, LC operative time, difficult gallbladder, intraoperative injuries and hemorrhage, post-LC complications, drainage placement and duration after LC, total hospital stay for LC, post-LC hospital stay, and hospitalization expenses. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the independent association between puncture site and perioperative outcomes. Results In univariate analyses, no significant differences were observed between the fundus and neck groups regarding intraoperative injuries or major postoperative complications. Compared with the neck group, the fundus group demonstrated significantly shorter LC operative time, a lower incidence of difficult gallbladder, fewer drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, reduced post-LC hospital stay, and lower hospitalization expenses (P < 0.05). In multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses, after adjusting for sex, age, body mass index (BMI), gallbladder neck stone impaction, interval between PTGD and LC, and TG18 severity grade, fundus-adjacent puncture remained independently associated with a lower risk of difficult gallbladder, reduced drainage placements and shorter drainage duration after LC, shorter post-LC and total hospital stays, and lower hospitalization expenses. In addition, fundus-adjacent puncture was associated with a 11.93 min reduction in LC operative time, although the association did not reach statistical significance (95%CI - 24.40 to 0.54; P = 0.061). Conclusions PTGD with puncture site adjacent to the gallbladder fundus is associated with improved surgical efficiency and reduced postoperative burden during subsequent LC. These findings suggest that fundus-adjacent puncture may be a favorable approach in clinical practice for optimizing patient outcomes following PTGD when technically feasible and clinically appropriate.

title: Leveraging traditional and advanced machine learning for comprehensive oncology data integration and outcome prediction.
abstract: Background Outcome prediction in neuro-oncology remains challenging due to heterogeneity in tumor biology, imaging characteristics, treatment response, and patient-specific clinical factors. Although molecular databases have advanced understanding of brain tumor biology, many datasets lack broader data necessary for generalizable predictive modeling. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are increasingly being explored to integrate these heterogeneous data sources and support precision neuro-oncology. Methods A narrative review was performed using PubMed and Embase to identify studies evaluating oncology databases, ML models, multimodal data integration, and AI applications relevant to neuro-oncology. Studies published between 2020 and 2026 were preferentially reviewed, with additional landmark studies included when relevant. Results Traditional ML approaches including regression-based models, random forests, support vector machines, and gradient boosting algorithms have been applied to survival prediction, recurrence classification, treatment response estimation, and molecular biomarker prediction using clinical, imaging, molecular, and population-level datasets. More advanced architectures including natural language processing, large language models, vision transformers, geometric deep learning, and graph neural networks have expanded the ability to analyze unstructured and multimodal data sources including radiology reports, histopathology slides, MRI volumes, molecular datasets, and electronic health records. Multimodal AI systems integrating imaging, molecular, histopathologic, clinical, and socioeconomic data frequently demonstrated improved predictive performance compared with single-modality models. However, widespread clinical implementation remains limited by dataset heterogeneity, limited external validation, interpretability concerns, and inconsistent representation across patient populations. Conclusions AI and ML approaches are increasingly capable of integrating complex neuro-oncology datasets in ways that more closely reflect real-world clinical decision-making. Although most current models remain investigational, multimodal AI frameworks may ultimately improve prognostic assessment, treatment stratification, and precision neuro-oncology care. Continued progress will require larger representative datasets, improved data harmonization, external validation, and clinically interpretable models.

title: RDB CycleGAN-CBAM: an integrated deep learning model for low-dose ct image denoising.
abstract: Computed Tomography (CT) is one of the largest contributors to radiation exposure from medical imaging, which can induce DNA damage and increase cancer risk. Reducing CT radiation dose to improve patient safety inherently increases image noise and artifacts. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown promise for unsupervised low-dose CT (LDCT) denoising. Building on this, RDBCycleGAN-CBAM, a CycleGAN-based model that integrates residual dense blocks (RDBs) and convolutional block attention modules (CBAM), was developed to effectively denoise quarter-dose CT images while preserving structural detail. The model was trained on unpaired quarter-dose and full-dose CT scans from the NIH-AAPM-Mayo dataset using adversarial (LSGAN), cycle-consistency, and identity losses. Evaluation on held-out test slices was performed using PSNR and SSIM as the primary image-quality metrics. The results demonstrate that the proposed RDBCycleGAN-CBAM method demonstrated improvements that were competitive with values reported in previous studies, achieving mean improvements of + 3.973 dB in PSNR and + 0.053 in SSIM relative to quarter-dose inputs. Shapiro-Wilk tests for PSNR and SSIM motivated the use of the nonparametric Wilcoxon signed-rank test, by which highly significant improvements across both metrics (PSNR and SSIM) were demonstrated. The very large rank-biserial correlation values (1.0) indicate that nearly all test images experienced substantial quality improvement. Furthermore, the narrow bootstrap confidence intervals for the mean differences suggest that these improvements are consistent across the dataset. These findings support further investigation of RDBCycleGAN-CBAM as a vendor-neutral image-domain denoising approach, while external validation and reader studies are required to establish its clinical utility and potential for dose reduction.

title: Learning from the unseen: synthetic data for scoliosis AI segmentation.
abstract: Purpose Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce. Methods We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset. Results On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable. Conclusion Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.
originalAbstract:
Purpose

Severe scoliosis remains challenging for 3D vertebral segmentation because annotated pathological computed tomography (CT) data are scarce.

Methods

We synthesize scoliosis-like CT volumes by jointly warping public healthy spine scans and labels and then train nnU-Net CNN and PRIMUS models under matched compute. We evaluate on in-house out-of-distribution (OOD) adolescent scoliosis CTs and the public Spine1K dataset.

Results

On 18 in-house adolescent scoliosis CTs, the best CNN setting increased mean Dice from 0.765 to 0.842 and vertebra success rate from 73.2 to 81.6%. In 55 surgeon-defined apical labels, mean Dice increased from 0.720 to 0.854. Spine1K performance remained high when synthetic data supplemented real scans; synthetic-only training was less stable.

Conclusion

Pathology-informed synthetic data improve robustness to severe scoliosis without new annotations or architecture changes. Code and interactive visualizations are available at: https://chepchikvaleri.github.io/synth-data-s/.

title: The clinical application value of mixed reality guidance in robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy for renal cancer.
abstract: Although robot-assisted laparoscopic radical nephrectomy (RAL-RN) has realized the benefits of minimally invasive surgery, it continues to face several key technical limitations, including the lack of integrated patient-specific three-dimensional anatomical navigation and insufficient real-time intraoperative navigation. While mixed reality (MR) technology has shown considerable potential in renal tumor surgery, its clinical application value specifically within the context of radical nephrectomy for renal cancer warrants further systematic evaluation. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and practical value of MR guidance in RAL-RN. A retrospective analysis was conducted of 74 patients who underwent RAL-RN between September 2021 and March 2024. Participants were categorized into two groups based on preoperative assessment methodology: an MR navigation group (n = 33) and a conventional imaging group (n = 41). All patients received non-contrast and triple-phase contrast-enhanced renal CT scans. The MR group utilized Hololens-based intraoperative anatomical reference with three-dimensional models reconstructed from preoperative CT data during Da Vinci robotic procedures. Perioperative outcomes, including baseline demographic and clinical characteristics, operative time, estimated blood loss, and postoperative complications, were compared between the two groups to assess the potential technical advantages of MR-guided navigation. The two groups showed comparable baseline characteristics (p > 0.05). The MR group exhibited significantly shorter operative time (161.15 ± 10.87 min versus 182.29 ± 12.40 min, p < 0.001), reduced blood loss (150.00 mL [interquartile range 140.00 to 165.00] versus 165.00 mL [150.00 to 165.00], p = 0.008), faster gastrointestinal function recovery (26.82 ± 4.17 h versus 28.93 ± 3.68 h, p = 0.024), earlier tube removal (5.00 days [4.00 to 5.00] versus 6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00], p < 0.001), and shorter postoperative hospitalization (6.00 days [6.00 to 7.00] versus 8.00 days [7.00 to 8.00], p < 0.001). No significant differences were observed in tumor staging, renal function parameters (postoperative and 12-month Scr and GFR), histopathological type, or complication rates (Clavien-Dindo grades 1 and 2) between groups (all p > 0.05). MR guidance was associated with shorter operative time and faster postoperative recovery in RAL-RN. However, given the non-randomized design, these findings should be regarded as preliminary and cannot establish causality. Prospective studies with standardized allocation and adequate follow-up are warranted to confirm the clinical value of MR guidance.

title: Vascular Phenotyping with Photoacoustic and Ultrasound Imaging in Cardiovascular Disease: Recent Innovations.
abstract: Purpose of review Photoacoustic and ultrasound imaging together resolve vascular structure, wall biomechanics, blood flow, oxygenation, and tissue composition without ionizing radiation or iodinated contrast. This review summarizes what each modality can now measure in patients and asks which of these measurements are close enough to clinical use to inform cardiovascular management decisions. Recent findings Recent advances have expanded photoacoustic imaging toward faster, higher-resolution functional vascular phenotyping, including clinically relevant biomarkers and co-registered ultrasound imaging. Ultrafast and super-resolution ultrasound now quantify vascular biomechanics, hemodynamics, and microvasculature, with ultrasound localization microscopy entering clinical studies. Wearable ultrasound has also been validated for blood-pressure monitoring across diverse care settings, alongside increasingly quantitative feature extraction. Summary Ultrasound and photoacoustic imaging provide complementary vascular information: ultrasound offers depth, speed, and continuous access, while photoacoustic imaging adds compositional and oxygenation contrast. Despite limitations in quantitative accuracy, imaging depth, and system standardization, emerging patient studies now span super-resolution vascular mapping, functional biomarkers, and wearable monitoring. Their integration offers a potential route toward continuous, operator-independent vascular phenotyping for clinical decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Prediction and Diagnosis of Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review.
abstract: This systematic review evaluates evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for prediction and diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR). The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, through June 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies on AI/ML-based prediction or diagnosis techniques for FGR, Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) or Small for gestational age (SGA) fetuses. The prediction model risk of bias assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used to perform data extraction and risk of bias assessment. Twenty-seven studies were eligible for inclusion. AI applications were biophysical (n = 10), Doppler-based (n = 10), clinical (n = 7), ultrasound (n = 7), MRI (n = 7), radiomics imaging (n = 10), cardiotocography (n = 10), genomics (n = 10), and metabolomics-based biomarker models (n = 10). The model performance was good, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC) of 0.71-0.91 and classification accuracies of 78.9-93.3%. Imaging and multimodal data-based models showed the highest predictive performance. The PROBAST assessment showed that the risk of bias was low for the participant, predictor and outcome domains, but the analytical domain raised methodological concerns; nine studies were low risk, 14 moderate and 4 high. The AI and ML models for FGR detection performed promisingly. Multimodal approaches that combine clinical, imaging and molecular data consistently outperform single modality models and constitute a major advance in precision obstetrics. However, there remains substantial heterogeneity, limited external validation and methodological issues. Future prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and real-world implementation research are needed for routine clinical adoption.

title: Normative Modeling of Amygdala Subfields and Disease-Specific Vulnerabilities Across Neurological Disorders.
abstract: As an integrative center of the limbic system, the amygdala and its subfields participate in diverse neural functions and demonstrate heterogeneous structural changes in various neurological disorders. In this study, three-dimensional T1-weighted MRI data from 22,258 healthy participants were analyzed using normative modeling to establish normative references for the volumes of the amygdala and its subfields. These models elucidated the developmental and aging curves of the amygdala and identified distinct ages at peak volume across subfields, ranging from 24.6 to 43.7 years. Based on these references, individual centile scores were calculated for 4132 patients with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, cerebral small vessel disease, multiple sclerosis, and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder. These centile scores not only captured disease-specific deviation patterns of the amygdala subfields but also demonstrated utility in disease classification. Moreover, the centile scores correlated with clinical measures of cognitive function, emotional state, and motor performance across disorders. These findings suggest that normative references of the amygdala subfields provide insights into cross-disease alteration patterns and offer potential neuroimaging biomarkers to aid differential diagnosis and clinical assessment.

abstract: Rationale and objectives The aim of this study is to evaluate the additional diagnostic value of CT Bone Reading software in detecting rib metastases on thoracic computed tomography in patients with breast cancer and to examine its effectiveness on lesion detection, evaluation time, and inter-reader agreement. Materials and methods This retrospective study included 110 patients with breast cancer and bone metastases who underwent both thoracic computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography-CT scans between January 2022 and January 2026. For lesion-level assessment, suspected rib lesions were also evaluated using available longitudinal follow-up imaging. Two radiologists independently evaluated conventional CT and CT Bone Reading images in separate reading sessions at least 2 weeks apart. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and Cohen's κ statistic. Results In lesion-based analysis with conventional CT, Reader 1 detected 510 lesions (81.6%) and Reader 2 detected 577 lesions (92.3%), while CT Bone Reading allowed for the detection of an additional 115 (22.5%) and 48 (8.3%) lesions for Readers 1 and 2, respectively. The additionally detected lesions demonstrated a non-uniform distribution, with a marked predominance in the mid-rib region (levels 5th-8th). CT Bone Reading-assisted evaluation enabled the detection of significantly smaller lesions compared to routine CT for both readers (Reader 1: 8.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; Reader 2: 7.0 mm vs 5.0 mm; P < 0.001 for both). Evaluation time was significantly decreased from 129.22 ± 27.22 s to 64.94 ± 17.16 s for Reader 1 and from 122.99 ± 26.04 s to 64.44 ± 18.71 s for Reader 2 (P < 0.001 for both). Inter-reader agreement was excellent for measurements obtained by CT Bone Reading-derived evaluation (ICC ≥0.965; κ ≥0.947). Conclusion CT Bone Reading software increases the detection rates of rib lesions, reduces interpretation times, and demonstrates excellent inter-reader reproducibility compared to conventional CT assessment, with less experienced readers achieving the highest incremental throughput. By providing a comprehensive and continuous view of the ribs, this technique has the potential to improve diagnostic performance without additional radiation exposure, particularly in anatomically complex regions such as the mid ribs. Ultimately, this approach can enhance workflow efficiency during routine clinical practices.

title: Barriers to artificial intelligence applications in ophthalmology: beyond diagnostic accuracy toward patient outcomes, workflow integration, ethics, and trust.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a major area of ophthalmic innovation, with a rapidly expanding literature, yet routine clinical adoption remains limited. Diagnostic accuracy alone is an insufficient marker of clinical value because even technically strong systems may fail to improve referral, follow-up, treatment, clinician workload, or health-system value. This focused narrative review examines the barriers that separate ophthalmic AI performance from real-world implementation. We reviewed ophthalmic AI literature indexed in PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, with emphasis on studies published from January 2018 to September 2026 and on prospective, randomized, real-world, economic, governance, and patient-centred evidence. We organize translation across four linked domains: algorithmic validity, clinical utility, workflow integration, and health-system value, with ethical governance and trust as cross-cutting requirements. Diabetic retinopathy screening now provides a concrete translational example spanning large-scale retrospective validation, prospective deployment, workflow implementation, and economic evaluation. We also consider how foundation models and large language models alter evidence requirements because outputs can depend on prompts, retrieved context, tools, and model versions. For glaucoma, retinal disease management, retinopathy of prematurity, anterior segment applications, and automated reporting, evidence remains less mature. The central challenge for ophthalmic AI is therefore no longer model development alone, but disciplined clinical translation, including prospective evaluation, operational workflow measurement, equity assessment, lifecycle monitoring, transparent governance, and trustworthy implementation.

title: Radiosynthesis and preliminary evaluation of [<sup>11</sup>C] and [<sup>18</sup>F] labelled lacosamide scaffolds for brain PET imaging.
abstract: This study summarizes the automated, transition-metal-free radiosynthesis approach for producing [ 11 C]LCM and its bioisosteric analogue [ 18 F]FLCM, along with preliminary pharmacological and preclinical evaluations of these radiotracers can act as potent brain imaging radiotracer candidates. Radiosynthesis was carried out using an automated synthesis module targeting the terminal 3-oxy site of lacosamide. Physicochemical properties, including hydrophilic behavior and plasma-protein binding profile, were evaluated. Translational validation was performed via in vivo PET/CT imaging and ex vivo biodistribution in healthy Wistar rats. The synthesis module yielded a radiotracer with high radiochemical yield and radiochemical purity. Specific activity was determined to be ~21 .7GBq/μmol for [ 11 C]LCM and ~6.76 GBq/μmole for [ 18 F]FLCM. Both radiotracers show favorable hydrophilic and low PPB profiles. In vivo PET scan and ex vivo study confirmed the brain uptake, renal and hepatic clearance, and minimal off-target uptake. The favorable pharmaceutical profiles establish a promising baseline, further rigorous in vitro receptor-affinity assays and dynamic brain imaging in an animal model are required to validate the translational diagnostic utility of these radiotracers.

title: Anchoring nanozymes on microneedles via nanotemplate sacrificial synthesis for glutathione detection.
abstract: Region-specific dysregulation of glutathione (GSH) reflects neuropsychiatric disorders and tumor progression. Microscale precision sampling combined with timely monitoring of GSH provides region-specific molecular information that may aid in disease diagnosis. To enable minimally invasive brain-compatible intraoperative detection of GSH within a limited surgical time window, we designed a 5 mm × 5 mm on-surface microneedle nanozyme sensing platform by adopting a seed-mediated sacrificial template method. The peroxidase (POD)-like nanozyme Prussian blue (PB) probe was grown in situ on a sacrificial ZIF-67 nanotemplate, which was first anchored to the microneedle surface via in situ nucleation to prevent probe detachment in tissue. The dense PB coating substantially increases the immobilization efficiency of GSH aptamers, enabling selective in situ sampling and accumulation of GSH on the nanozyme. This creates a redox antagonistic effect between PB and GSH, which enables the platform to exhibit high selectivity toward GSH over common redox-active interferents. The quantitative concentration range of 271.3-900 μM (R 2 > 0.99) for GSH is demonstrated in a simulated gelatinous tissue, and GSH levels in brain interstitial fluid could be distinguished within 20 min. Less biopsy tissue and shorter analysis time may help minimize tissue damage and could provide timely intraoperative molecular information, potentially complementing histopathology.

title: Multimodal visual question answering in neuro-oncology and gastroenterology: A domain-specific feasibility study.
abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) requires models to combine image content with the clinical intent expressed by a question, yet domain-specific resources and controlled analyses of modality use remain limited. This study introduces two expert-validated Med-VQA datasets for brain tumor MRI and gastrointestinal endoscopy and evaluates a dual-stream architecture that combines BERT question representations and ViT image features through Modular Co-Attention on Attention (MCAoA). The model formulates answer prediction as closed-vocabulary classification and is assessed through overall, question-type, disease-class, baseline, ablation, and usability analyses. The complete fine-tuned model with product fusion achieved accuracies of 80.86% (WUPS 81.32%) on the brain tumor dataset and 75.95% (WUPS 76.77%) on the gastrointestinal dataset. It exceeded the question-only and image-only baselines by 23.86 and 43.16 percentage points, respectively, on brain tumor MRI, and by 18.54 and 35.92 percentage points on gastrointestinal endoscopy. Product fusion provided a small but consistent advantage over concatenation, while end-to-end encoder fine-tuning improved accuracy over frozen encoders on both datasets. A complementary study with clinical experts indicated positive perceived usability in a controlled setting. These findings show that performance cannot be reproduced from either modality alone and support the complementary use of image and question information. However, the ablations establish modality-level dependence rather than spatially correct anatomical grounding, which requires targeted counterfactual and attribution-based evaluation.

title: Clinical-context guidance and hyperbolic prototype learning for long-tailed radiology report generation.
abstract: Automated radiology report generation (RRG) can reduce the reporting burden, but existing methods remain limited in their ability to integrate clinical context effectively at the feature level. They also struggle with long-tailed disease distributions, which can hinder recognition of infrequent findings. To address these issues, CSMH-RRG, a clinically guided framework that integrates clinical semantic modulation (CSM) and hyperbolic prototype-based classification (HPC), is proposed. The CSM module conditions postencoder visual representations on patient-specific clinical context through semantic injection and channel recalibration. The HPC module represents multiple disease states as learnable prototypes on the Poincaré ball and converts predicted states into disease-state tokens for report generation. Under the primary MIMIC-CXR protocol, CSMH-RRG achieved a BLEU-4 score of 0.262 and a diseasewise macro CheXbert F1 score of 0.564, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical factuality metrics while maintaining comparable BLEU-4 performance to the best-performing baseline. When transferred from MIMIC-CXR to IU X-ray without fine tuning, it achieved a BLEU-4 score of 0.118 and a CE F1 score of 0.289. Specifically, in the MIMIC-CXR frequency-stratified classifier analysis, CSMH-RRG increased tail-group macro F1 from 35.5% to 41.4% relative to the linear baseline. Head-group macro F1 also increased from 72.1% to 73.5%. These results indicate that CSMH-RRG supports report generation and improves frequency-sensitive disease-state prediction within the evaluated benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/tinkerbellqwq/CSMH-RRG.

title: <sup>177</sup>Lu-Prostate-specific Membrane Antigen Prior to Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy in Oligorecurrent Prostate Cancer: Secondary and Exploratory End Point Results from the Randomized Phase 2 LUNAR Trial.
abstract: The phase 2 randomized LUNAR trial previously demonstrated that neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 before stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) significantly improved progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with oligorecurrent hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (orHSPC). We report updated efficacy and safety outcomes with extended follow-up. Patients with prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT)-detected orHSPC and one to five metastatic lesions amenable to SBRT were randomized 1:1 to SBRT alone or two cycles of neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 followed by SBRT. The primary end point was PFS, defined as new lesions on PSMA PET/CT, initiation of salvage hormonal therapy, or death. Secondary end points included hormonal therapy-free survival (HT-FS) and 24-mo progression-free status. Exploratory end points included polymetastatic PFS (poly-PFS), castration-resistant disease-free survival (CRFS), and conventional imaging progression-free survival (CT-PFS). Between September 2022 and November 2023, 92 patients were randomized to SBRT alone (n = 47) or 177 Lu-PNT2002 plus SBRT (n = 45). At a median follow-up of 31.9 mo, 177 Lu-PNT2002 significantly improved PFS (median 17.6 vs 7.4 mo; hazard ratio [HR] 0.38, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.23-0.61; p < 0.001) and HT-FS (HR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.34-0.95; p = 0.03). Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant 177 Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

Exploratory analyses demonstrated improved poly-PFS (HR 0.28, 95% CI = 0.08-1.03; p = 0.04), CRFS (HR 0.13, 95% CI = 0.02-1.10; p = 0.03), and CT-PFS (HR 0.46, 95% CI = 0.19-1.09; p = 0.07). No new safety signals were observed. With extended follow-up, neoadjuvant <sup>177</sup>Lu-PNT2002 before SBRT produced durable improvements in PFS and HT-FS. While poly-PFS, CRFS, and CT-PFS were exploratory end points, their improvement provides hypothesis-generating evidence that the addition of radioligand therapy to SBRT may alter disease trajectory beyond delaying PSMA PET/CT-detected recurrence.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Triage in Primary Care: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applicability.
abstract: Aim To map artificial intelligence (AI) systems developed for triage in primary care and describe their characteristics, performance and clinical applicability. Methods A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. PubMed, MEDLINE (via Ovid), Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL (via EBSCOhost), IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library were searched until March 14th 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data on system characteristics, triage function, performance, validation, safety, equity and implementation. Each system was charted by triage function and by whether it was patient-facing, clinician-facing or fully automated. Results Seventeen studies were included, published between 2013 and 2026 across 12 countries (14/17 high-income). Most were clinician-facing decision support (14/17), three had a patient-facing component and none were autonomous. Diagnostic or screening triage was the most common function (n = 7), followed by prioritisation (n = 4) and referral routing (n = 4). Only two performed urgency classification or self-triage. As a clinician aid, AI improved performance (fundus accuracy 82.8 % to 91.1 %; dermoscopy management sensitivity 72.9 % to 94.2 %), but standalone models sometimes fell below clinicians. Reported accuracy ranged from 41.2 % to 98.28 % and AUROC from 0.65 to 0.90, on heterogeneous outcomes. Validation was mostly internal (11/17), external in four. None reported a prospective randomised comparison or measured patient outcomes. Conclusion AI triage in primary care is concentrated on clinician-facing diagnostic and referral tasks and is most valuable for augmenting clinician workflows, particularly non-specialists. The evidence base remains immature, constrained by internal validation, unreliable reference standards, sparse equity assessment and absent prospective outcome data. Future work should prioritise prospective, outcome-anchored evaluation, with attention to safety and equity.

title: An unusual Case of p63/p40 Negative Myoepithelial cell-Rich Parotid Pleomorphic Adenoma.
abstract: Pleomorphic adenoma is the most common benign salivary gland neoplasm; however, myoepithelial-rich variants with unusual immunophenotypes are rare and pose diagnostic challenges. We report a myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma of the parotid gland in a 23-year-old male presenting with a slowly enlarging, painless infraauricular swelling. Grossly, the lesion was well-circumscribed and encapsulated. Histopathology revealed predominantly spindle, oval, and plasmacytoid myoepithelial cells embedded in densely hyalinized fibromyxoid stroma, with sparse ductal structures. The paucity of ducts and prominent myoepithelial proliferation closely mimicked myoepithelioma. Immunohistochemically, tumor cells showed diffuse expression of S100, pan-cytokeratin, and high-molecular-weight cytokeratin, supporting epithelial and myoepithelial differentiation. EMA and CD117 selectively highlighted the sparse ductal structures, providing a crucial diagnostic clue. Notably, the tumor was completely negative for p40, p63, and smooth muscle actin, representing an unusual immunophenotype for pleomorphic adenoma. Despite the absence of conventional myoepithelial markers, integration of the subtle residual ductal morphology and complementary immunoprofile established the diagnosis of myoepithelial-rich pleomorphic adenoma, excluding myoepithelioma and other salivary gland neoplasms. The patient recovered uneventfully after surgery and remained recurrence-free at six months. This case expands the immunohistochemical spectrum of pleomorphic adenoma and highlights that the absence of p40 and p63 expression should not preclude its diagnosis. Comprehensive immunohistochemical assessment, interpreted alongside meticulous histomorphological evaluation, is essential to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in these uncommon tumors.

title: Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
abstract: Introduction Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure. Methods A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure. Results A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity. Conclusion We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

title: Assessing the incidence of retinal hemorrhage in pediatric patients following COVID-19 vaccination.
abstract: Background Retinal hemorrhages (RHs) are a cardinal finding in abusive head trauma (AHT) for which a broad differential diagnosis is appropriate to consider. The frequency of COVID-19 vaccination and reports of subsequent ocular manifestations have led to the consideration of whether COVID-19 vaccination should be included in the RH differential. This study aimed to investigate the frequency of RH following COVID-19 vaccination in children. Methods In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination. Results Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination. Conclusions RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

In this single-center, retrospective, observational cohort study, we reviewed the medical records of children ≤8 years of age who received a COVID-19 vaccine from July 1, 2020, to July 1, 2024, and underwent a fundus examination within 21 days of vaccination. The main outcome measure was incidence and characteristics of RH on fundus examination.

Results

Of 17,926 children vaccinated during this period, 203 subjects met inclusion criteria and underwent 212 unique examinations, with mean age of 4.56 years (0-8) at the time of first examination. Twenty examinations were also in the setting of prior COVID-19 infection. No examinations revealed RH. Based on Hanley's rule of zero incidence, the 95th percentile upper limit of incidence of RH after COVID-19 vaccination is 4.11% at 7 days, 2.04% at 14 days, and 1.42% at 21 days following vaccination.

Conclusions

RHs were not seen in any children within 21 days of COVID-19 vaccination. This suggests that RH is rare following COVID-19 vaccination and perhaps of little relevance to the differential diagnosis of RH in the evaluation for AHT.

title: Intraoperative and radiographic indicators of extraocular muscle aberrancy in syndromic craniosynostosis.
abstract: Background Strabismus is common in syndromic craniosynostosis, often attributed to abnormal extraocular muscle (EOM) trajectory, and orbital anatomy. Absent EOMs have been reported, but the spectrum of primary dysgenesis remains poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to characterize the range of EOM dysgenesis in a large cohort that had undergone strabismus surgery. Methods The medical records of patients with syndromic craniosynostosis treated at Boston Children's Hospital (2010-2023) were reviewed retrospectively to identify all cases with neuroimaging and history of strabismus surgery. Genetic testing results and EOM abnormalities noted on neuroimaging or during surgery were recorded. Imaging was reviewed to determine presence of each EOM. Superior oblique muscle (SO) size was classified as "normal" if its transverse diameter was at least one-half that of the adjacent medial rectus muscle. Results A total of 47 patients with syndromic craniosynostosis had undergone strabismus surgery, of whom 43 had available neuroimaging. Syndromic associations were as follows: 21 patients with Apert, 10 with Crouzon, 6 with Pfeiffer, 5 with Saethre-Chotzen, and 1 with Muenke. Rectus and inferior oblique muscles were universally present. SO size was normal in only 15 of 86 eyes (17%). EOM aberrancies were noted intraoperatively in 15 of 43 operative cases (35%), including diaphanous insertions, bifid or fused rectus muscles, and posterior inferior oblique insertions. Results of genetic testing were available for 26 patients, 24 of whom had FGFR2 mutations, including all 10 (of 15) patients with intraoperatively noted EOM aberrancies who underwent genetic testing. Conclusions In this cohort with syndromic craniosynostosis, thin-section or high-resolution orbital imaging demonstrated presence of all rectus muscles even when insertions were diaphanous. The SO was hypoplastic in 83%. Aberrancies noted intraoperatively in 35% likely underestimate the true incidence, because evaluation was limited to muscles targeted for surgery.

title: Abnormal left ventricular mass as a prognostic marker for outcomes in infants and children with cirrhosis.
abstract: Background/aims Cirrhotic cardiomyopathy (CCM), a clinically consequential comorbidity of cirrhosis, remains undefined and underappreciated in children. This study aimed to characterize myocardial structural, functional, morphometric, and histopathologic features in pediatric cirrhosis and objectively derive a reliable echocardiographic (2DE) metric to predict perioperative adverse events, including mortality. Methods 2DE, morphometry, histopathology, and vasoactive-inotropic score (VIS) were compared between children with (n=226) and without (n=160) cirrhosis listed for liver transplantation (LT) over 2011-2021. Discriminatory performance of left ventricular mass index (height) 2.7 (LVMI g/m 2.7 ) for predicting waitlist decompensation, composite serious adverse events post liver transplant and mortality was assessed using ROC analysis, with AUCs and optimal thresholds compared against PELD-Cr/MELD scores. Results LV mass was significantly higher in children with cirrhosis on 2DE and necropsy specimens compared to non-cirrhotic controls, with ∼25% demonstrating LV hypertrophy, with OR of 6.9 [CI 3,16], p< 0.0001. In the cirrhotic cohort, LVMI correlated with vasoactive needs under stress of LT (p <0.001) and was significantly higher in patients with WLD, CSAE, and non-survivors. In cirrhosis, LVMI values ≥ 88 g/m 2.7 , ≥ 91 g/m 2.7, and ≥ 95 g/m 2.7 were independently associated with WLD, CSAE, and mortality, when adjusting for PELD-Cr/MELD, bilirubin, and INR (p <0.01). Combining LVMI + PELD-Cr/MELD significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD in discriminating both WLD and CSAE, whereas LVMI alone significantly outperformed PELD-Cr/MELD for CSAE and was comparable for WLD. All three models performed comparably in discriminating death. Conclusion LVMI is a strong predictor of morbidity and mortality, serving as a prognostic marker in children with cirrhosis. Incorporating LVMI into PELD-Cr/MELD may enhance risk stratification and organ allocation.

title: The Prognostic Value of Entropy from T1 Mapping in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
abstract: Background The prognostic value of left ventricular (LV) entropy from T1 mapping in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains unexplored. Study design and methods This prospective study enrolled patients with PAH who underwent cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) within 72h of right heart catheterization (RHC). Myocardial native T1, extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and entropy were calculated in mid-ventricular short-axis slice. The primary endpoint was defined as all-cause mortality or lung transplantation. Outcomes were further analyzed across groups stratified by survival status using Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis. Results A total of 312 patients were analyzed over a median follow-up of 36.10 months, with 59 deaths. Elevated LV entropy was positively correlated with log-transformed NT-proBNP, right ventricular (RV) end-systolic, end-diastolic volume indices, LV native T1 and ECV, and inversely correlated with RV ejection fraction (all P < 0.01). LV entropy did not differ significantly across etiological subgroups, whereas LV entropy without IPs was higher in congenital heart disease-associated PAH. Both LV entropy ≥8.60 and LV entropy without IPs ≥8.30 independently predicted all-cause mortality (HR, 2.207; 95% CI, 1.324-3.678; P = 0.002; and HR, 2.357; 95% CI, 1.405-3.955; P = 0.001, respectively) and were associated with reduced survival (both log-rank P < 0.005). Adding LV entropy improved ESC models (χ²: 55.79 to 60.61, C-statistic: 0.782 to 0.801) and ESC-CMR models (χ²: 35.31 to 41.77, C-statistic: 0.805 to 0.813). Conclusions Elevated LV entropy was related to disease severity, RV dysfunction, and adverse clinical outcomes, and served as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients with PAH. Registration URL: https://www. Clinicaltrials gov; Unique identifier: ChiCTR1800019314 and ChiCTR1900025518.

title: Automatic 3D TOF-MRA Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation using SAM-Guided Multi-View Decoding Network.
abstract: Background Deep learning-based aneurysm segmentation using 3D time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA) offers promising non-invasive screening, but its accuracy and generalizability remain limited. Purpose To develop a deep learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection and segmentation on MRA, and evaluate its multicenter performance against the digital subtraction angiography (DSA) gold standard and radiologists of varying experience. Materials and methods MRA images from patients suspected of harboring unruptured intracranial aneurysms were retrospectively collected from Jinhua Municipal Central Hospital for model development. An external test set, with DSA as the reference standard, was gathered from Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Manual segmentation of cerebral arteries and aneurysms was performed using 3D-Slicer software. Performance was evaluated via Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), sensitivity, and F1-score, and compared against independent clinical evaluations from radiologists with different experience levels. Results The internal dataset comprised 1,560 patients (1,554 aneurysms), including 421 patients (522 aneurysms) for testing. The external test set included 208 patients (224 aneurysms). On the internal test set, the model achieved a lesion-level sensitivity of 86.0% (95% CI: 82.8 - 88.7), a precision of 87.4% (95% CI: 84.2, 90.0), and a DSC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84, 0.90). On the independent external test set, the model demonstrated robust generalizability with a sensitivity of 83.4% (95% CI: 75.9, 88.0) and a DSC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79, 0.87). The model achieved an overall detection F1-score of 86.7, significantly outperforming junior radiologists (P <.001) and was comparable to mid-level radiologists (P >.05), with an average processing time of approximately 72seconds per exam. Conclusion The proposed deep learning model demonstrated robust multicenter performance for intracranial aneurysm detection and segmentation. Achieving diagnostic accuracy comparable to mid-level radiologists, it holds potential as an efficient assistive tool for MRA interpretation in clinical workflows.

title: Predictive Modeling of Clinically Apparent Shoulder Periprosthetic Joint Infection (PJI).
abstract: Introduction The first International Consensus Meeting (ICM) definition of shoulder periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) introduced a tiered framework of PJI categories based on weighting of minor criteria for those cases not having major criteria of Definite infection. The selection of minor criteria and weightings was based on expert opinion and limited available evidence. The purpose of this study was to use prospective, multicenter data to develop a predictive model for clinically apparent shoulder PJI to inform a more evidence-based understanding of minor criteria and PJI categories. Methods Prospective data were collected on 861 consecutive revision shoulder arthroplasty cases within the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty and PJI Multicenter Research Group. Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis and intra-articular purulence were identified as pathognomonic indicators of infection (major criteria) and used as the primary outcome for multivariable analysis. Logistic regression modeling was performed, with model specification guided by information criteria. Variable selection emphasized optimal model fit while balancing complexity, focusing on: (1) markers of host inflammatory response, (2) universally available and commonly utilized diagnostic tests, (3) minimizing the total number of variables, and (4) preserving model usability despite missing data. Results Among 861 cases, 97 shoulders (11%) met the outcome of interest (sinus tract or intra-articular purulence). The final model incorporated seven variables spanning clinical findings, laboratory values, imaging, intraoperative assessment, and microbiology. These variables were erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP), radiographic humeral osteolysis, synovial neutrophils ≥70% or positive frozen section (≥5 polymorphonuclear cells in ≥5 high-powered fields), intraoperative humeral loosening, and ≥2 positive cultures with the same organism. The apparent concordance statistic in the development cohort was 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.94). A nomogram was subsequently developed to estimate the probability of PJI, defined by the presence of a sinus tract or intra-articular purulence. Conclusion Using prospective, multicenter data, this study proposes a seven-factor nomogram to estimate the probability of clinically apparent shoulder PJI. The model showed strong apparent discrimination for clinically apparent infection in the development cohort. External validation will be necessary to confirm performance, and consensus will be required to establish weighting and diagnostic thresholds for tiers of non-definite shoulder PJI.

The first International Consensus Meeting (ICM) definition of shoulder periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) introduced a tiered framework of PJI categories based on weighting of minor criteria for those cases not having major criteria of Definite infection. The selection of minor criteria and weightings was based on expert opinion and limited available evidence. The purpose of this study was to use prospective, multicenter data to develop a predictive model for clinically apparent shoulder PJI to inform a more evidence-based understanding of minor criteria and PJI categories.

Methods

Prospective data were collected on 861 consecutive revision shoulder arthroplasty cases within the American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) Revision Shoulder Arthroplasty and PJI Multicenter Research Group. Presence of a sinus tract communicating with the prosthesis and intra-articular purulence were identified as pathognomonic indicators of infection (major criteria) and used as the primary outcome for multivariable analysis. Logistic regression modeling was performed, with model specification guided by information criteria. Variable selection emphasized optimal model fit while balancing complexity, focusing on: (1) markers of host inflammatory response, (2) universally available and commonly utilized diagnostic tests, (3) minimizing the total number of variables, and (4) preserving model usability despite missing data.

Results

Among 861 cases, 97 shoulders (11%) met the outcome of interest (sinus tract or intra-articular purulence). The final model incorporated seven variables spanning clinical findings, laboratory values, imaging, intraoperative assessment, and microbiology. These variables were erythema, unexpected wound drainage, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) or C-reactive protein (CRP), radiographic humeral osteolysis, synovial neutrophils ≥70% or positive frozen section (≥5 polymorphonuclear cells in ≥5 high-powered fields), intraoperative humeral loosening, and ≥2 positive cultures with the same organism. The apparent concordance statistic in the development cohort was 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.94). A nomogram was subsequently developed to estimate the probability of PJI, defined by the presence of a sinus tract or intra-articular purulence.

Conclusion

Using prospective, multicenter data, this study proposes a seven-factor nomogram to estimate the probability of clinically apparent shoulder PJI. The model showed strong apparent discrimination for clinically apparent infection in the development cohort. External validation will be necessary to confirm performance, and consensus will be required to establish weighting and diagnostic thresholds for tiers of non-definite shoulder PJI.

title: Artificial intelligence-supported diabetic retinopathy screening in Tanzania: a randomised controlled trial.
abstract: Background Non-attendance after referral from screening is one of the major challenges for diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for the identification of diabetic retinopathy can provide point-of-screening results and therefore enable immediate counselling. We aimed to investigate whether AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy who attended the central ophthalmology referral clinic when compared with standard diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human grading and telephone counselling. Methods This two-arm, parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial was conducted at non-communicable disease or diabetic clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Eligible participants (aged ≥18 years) had diabetes and attended diabetic retinopathy screening. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling (the AI-intervention group) or standard-of-care diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human retinal image assessment and telephone counselling (the standard-of-care group). Participants had retinal photographs taken of both eyes. Images from the AI-intervention group were submitted to the AI software, and these participants were given their screening result (non-referable, referable, or ungradable) plus face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room, with a referral to the central ophthalmology clinic if the AI output was referable or ungradable. Participants in the standard-of-care group received their screening result, along with appropriate counselling, by telephone a few weeks later. The primary outcome was attendance at the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks of screening among participants classified by masked UK-certified graders as having true referable diabetic retinopathy. This trial was registered with the ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN18317152, and is complete. Findings Between March 8, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, 2439 participants were assessed for eligibility and 2378 were enrolled, of whom 1192 were randomly assigned to the AI-intervention group and 1186 to the standard-of-care group. 904 participants had true referable diabetic retinopathy, comprising 437 in the AI-intervention group and 467 in the standard-of-care group. Of the participants in the AI-intervention group, 157 (35·9%) of 437 attended the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks, compared with 85 (18·2%) of 467 in the standard-of-care group, an absolute difference of 17·7 percentage points (95% CI 12·0-23·4; odds ratio 2·52 [95% CI 1·86-3·42]; p<0·0001). Interpretation AI-supported screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy that attended the central ophthalmology clinic after screening compared with the standard of care in Tanzania. Such AI-enabled screening pathways have the potential to improve diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. title: Performance uncertainty in medical image analysis: A large-scale investigation of confidence intervals.
abstract: Performance uncertainty quantification is essential for reliable validation and eventual clinical translation of medical imaging artificial intelligence (AI). Confidence intervals (CIs) play a central role in this process by indicating how precise a reported performance estimate is. Yet, due to the limited amount of work examining CI behavior in medical imaging, the community remains largely unaware of how many diverse CI methods exist and how they behave in specific settings. The purpose of this study is to close this gap. To this end, we conducted a large-scale empirical analysis across a total of 24 segmentation and classification tasks, using 19 trained models per task group, a broad spectrum of commonly used performance metrics, multiple aggregation strategies, and several widely adopted CI methods. Reliability (coverage) and precision (width) of each CI method were estimated across all settings to characterize their dependence on study characteristics. Our analysis revealed five principal findings: (1) the sample size required for reliable CIs varies from a few dozens to several thousands of cases depending on study parameters; (2) CI behavior is strongly affected by the choice of performance metric; (3) aggregation strategy substantially influences the reliability of CIs, e.g. they require more observations for macro than for micro; (4) the machine learning problem (segmentation versus classification) modulates these effects; (5) different CI methods are not equally reliable and precise depending on the use case. Finally, we derived practical implications of this study in the form of a decision tree which shall prove useful to the community. This paves the way for future consensus guidelines on reporting performance uncertainty.

title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches.
abstract: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations. It is increasingly recognized that the variability in tumor behaviour is incompletely captured using traditional systems. Contemporary advances have expanded tumor stratification beyond starting WHO grading, providing a more comprehensive framework for understanding tumor biology. Molecular profiling has identified independent biological classification systems and molecular signatures that capture important prognostic information beyond histopathology. Magnetic resonance imaging-based analyses and radiomics have enabled non-invasive characterization of tumor phenotype and growth potential. Therapeutically, surgical resection and radiation therapy remain the foundation of management, with evolving paradigms emphasizing maximal safe resection and risk-adapted radiotherapy strategies informed by integrated tumor characteristics. Systemic therapies have historically shown limited efficacy; however, recent efforts are shifting toward biomarker-driven, precision approaches guided by molecular alterations. Future directions focus on integrating multimodal data into unified, clinically actionable models that more accurately predict recurrence, progression, and treatment response. Such approaches aim to move beyond parallel classification systems toward individualized management strategies, ultimately advancing meningioma care into a precision-based paradigm.

title: Investigation of CardioFreeze Motion Correction for Cardiac PET/CT.
abstract: Background Cardiac imaging with positron emission tomography and computed tomography (PET/CT) is a principal technique in the diagnosis and prognostication of coronary artery disease. PET/CT image quality can be negatively impacted by patient, cardiac, and respiratory motion. Methods We evaluated images from 102 patients clinically referred for cardiac rest/stress Rb-82 PET/CT myocardial perfusion imaging. Patient images were processed with a prototype data-driven motion detection algorithm and stratified by motion severity. Images were subjected to cardiac (CS) or cardiac and respiratory (CD) motion correction via a novel reconstruction tool. Validated image quality markers including target-to-background ratio (TBR) were assessed between corrected and non-corrected images and analyzed via student's t-tests. Results The motion detection algorithm identified 36 (35.3%) patients with significant motion. title: Multicenter Evaluation of a Deep Learning Model for Automatic Contouring of Cardiac Substructures in Adults.
abstract: Purpose Efficient delineation of cardiac substructures is essential for assessing radiation-induced cardiac toxicity in thoracic radiotherapy. We clinically evaluated a deep learning model designed for automated segmentation of these structures. Methods and materials The model built in collaboration with XXX (XXX) generated 21 cardiac substructures (whole heart, chambers, coronary arteries, valves, and great vessels). Five radiation oncologists rated raw contours on thirty contrast-enhanced CTs from two institutions using a 4-point Likert scale (3 = no correction, 2 = minor/moderate correction, 1 = major correction, 0 = not performed) and applied corrections when needed. Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distances (HD95) were computed to compare model versus reference contours, clinician-corrected versus reference contours, and model versus STAPLE contours. Results Of 630 structures, 93.8% were scored either 3 or ≥2, and 6.2% received 1 by at least one clinician. For the coronary arteries (210 structures), 88.5% were scored either 3 or ≥ 2. Contour generation took approximately 1 min, with a median review and correction time of 7.0 min per CT (IQR, 5.8-9.8). The median DSC between the model and reference contours was 1.0 across all structures, while it ranged from 0.92 to 1.0 for clinician-corrected versus reference contours. Overall, HD95 was below 5 mm, for both clinicians versus reference and model versus STAPLE. Conclusions The deep learning model provided satisfactory segmentation of cardiac substructures on contrast-enhanced CT, including coronary arteries. Its integration into a widely adopted treatment planning system lays the foundation for broad clinical implementation.

title: Inadvertent Coronary Sinus Cannulation During Central Venous Catheter Placement in a Liver Transplant Recipient with Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava: A Case Report.
abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is the most common thoracic venous anomaly and is usually asymptomatic. Central venous catheterization through a PLSVC can be challenging, and inadvertent advancement of catheters into the coronary sinus may result in arrhythmias, perforation, thrombosis, or inaccurate hemodynamic measurements. We report a case of coronary sinus cannulation by a left internal jugular dialysis catheter in a liver transplant recipient with previously unrecognized PLSVC. Initial chest radiography suggested catheter termination within a duplicated left superior vena cava; however, intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated the catheter tip within the coronary sinus. The catheter was withdrawn under direct echocardiographic guidance, avoiding potential complications. This case highlights the utility of intraoperative TEE for definitive localization of central venous catheters in patients with anomalous thoracic venous anatomy.
